references.text: The parallel text in Exodus where the Ten Commandments are first given, with the same prohibition against killing.
The basis for the prohibition against murder: whoever sheds human blood shall have their own blood shed, because humans are created in God's image.
The law that anyone who kills a person must die, an elaboration of the commandment against murder.
Provisions stating that a murderer must die and that no ransom may be accepted for the life of a murderer.
Jesus quotes this commandment and expands it to include anger toward a brother and insulting words.
Jesus cites the commandment against killing as part of the commandments that must be kept to receive eternal life.
Paul quotes the commandment against killing as one of the commandments summarized in the commandment to love.
James refers to the commandment against killing to show that whoever breaks one commandment is guilty of breaking the whole law.
